subject: Clarify invoice routing & tax evidence for Azure co-sell transaction - CloudServe
messages:
From: Samantha O'Neill <samantha.oneill@cloudserve.com>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
Cc: accounts.payments@cloudserve.com
Date: 2027-02-14T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Question on invoice recipient and withholding for Azure co-sell

Hi Roahn (and team),

Apologies for the message first thing — our finance team received the Azure Marketplace settlement for our recent co-sell (invoice #4321) and they're asking a couple of things before they can clear payment:

- The invoice Redwood received from Azure lists CloudServe as the billed party, but the invoice PDF attached to the settlement does not show our VAT ID or the tax residency details we provided during procurement.
- Our local AP requires confirmation whether the marketplace invoicing counts as a pass-through (CloudServe invoices end customer and remits to Redwood) or whether Azure is acting as the vendor of record and paid Redwood directly. This affects whether we need to provide a W-9/W-8 or if the VAT reverse-charge applies.

Can someone from Redwood confirm the correct routing and what evidence you need from us (signed W-9 / W-8BEN-E / tax residency certificate)? I attached the invoice PDF we received from Azure.

Thanks,
Samantha O'Neill
Head of Finance, CloudServe Ltd
attachments: azure_invoice_4321.pdf (PDF, 412 KB)

From: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
To: Samantha O'Neill <samantha.oneill@cloudserve.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-14T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question on invoice recipient and withholding for Azure co-sell

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear note and the invoice. Quick summary from our side so finance can proceed: 

1) Marketplace role: For this transaction we were the provider of record to Azure (Azure billed CloudServe and remitted settlement to Redwood). That means Azure acts as the platform seller to you and we received settlement from Azure, not a direct invoice to Redwood from CloudServe.

2) Tax treatment: Because the invoice was issued to CloudServe by Azure, your AP should treat this as a marketplace-billed purchase. VAT handling depends on your country:
   - If CloudServe is VAT-registered in the EU and provided a VAT ID to Azure, reverse-charge may apply (no VAT charged on the Azure invoice, but you self-account).
   - If Azure charged VAT on the invoice, that is for the marketplace transaction and the VAT line should be on the Azure PDF.

3) W-8/W-9: Those forms are typically used for U.S. tax withholding when the marketplace settlement flows differently (e.g., direct payments to vendor). Since Azure billed you and settled with us, the withholding risk is low, but sometimes reseller withholding occurs at your local level. If CloudServe's treasury is requesting evidence, we can accept a copy of the W-9 (if you are a US entity) or W-8BEN-E if US withholding is in scope — however, having the VAT registration / tax residency certificate is more relevant for VAT treatment.

Action items: 
- Samantha: please confirm CloudServe's VAT ID and country of registration (send VAT cert if available).
- Vanessa: can you confirm whether our Marketplace onboarding records show CloudServe as the billed party and whether Azure recorded a VAT ID on their side?
- Karthik: if CloudServe needs a signed vendor-side attestation (redwood side) to show we're the payee for settlement, can you draft a short confirmation for AP?

I'll loop back after Vanessa/Karthik confirm.

Best,
Roahn Mehta
Head of Partnerships (acting) — Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

On Mon, 14 Feb 2027 at 09:05, rohan_mehta@redwood.ai wrote:
> Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear note and the invoice. Quick summary from our side so finance can proceed: 

Thanks, Roahn — checked the marketplace onboarding dashboard and Azure's settlement metadata. My notes:

- Azure's invoice metadata shows CloudServe Ltd as the billed customer (so AP should reconcile to that). We do have CloudServe's VAT ID in our onboarding profile, but sometimes the marketplace does not display it on the PDF if the seller-entered field was omitted.
- The settlement we received included a line item that indicates a standard marketplace commission; there was no U.S. withholding taken by Azure on this settlement.
- If CloudServe's AP wants Redwood to confirm we are the recipient of the settlement from Azure, we can provide a brief vendor confirmation letter. I attached a draft confirmation and a simplified flow diagram that shows Azure -> CloudServe (billing) and Azure -> Redwood (settlement).

Attachments: redwood_marketplace_flow.png (PNG, 84 KB), vendor_confirmation_draft.docx (DOCX, 12 KB)

Samantha — for your AP you can: 
- Provide CloudServe's VAT cert (if EU VAT is relevant) or invoice-backed evidence from Azure.
- If they'll only accept a vendor-side W-9/W-8, we are happy to accept a signed copy for our records and will countersign if needed (but that form does not change how Azure processed VAT at settlement).

Vanessa Ortiz
Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference

Samantha — quick follow up from Redwood finance (copied policies and next steps):

- Redwood can provide a signed vendor confirmation letter (PDF) that states: Redwood received settlement for invoice 4321 from Azure and that Azure invoiced CloudServe as the billed customer. This note is suitable for AP reconciliation and usually clears bank hold flags.
- If CloudServe's treasury insists on a W-9 / W-8BEN-E, please upload the signed document to the HubSpot deal folder (link below) or send via secure email. We will add it to our vendor file.
- VAT: If reverse charge applies in your jurisdiction, your AP must account for it on their VAT return — the invoice we observed does not have a Redwood VAT charge line. If Azure charged VAT, it will appear on the Azure PDF and CloudServe should reclaim per local rules.
